item.title: android/skills
item.description:
Android skills

Android skills are a dedicated repository of AI-optimized, modular instructions and resources, to help agents better understand and execute specific patterns that follow the best practices and guidance on Android development from developer.android.com.

Android skills follow the open-standard agent skills - markdown files (SKILL.md) that provide a technical specification of a task, and ground LLMs with information on specialized domains and workflows.

Our Android skill development focuses on use cases and workflows where evaluations show LLMs underperform. We aren't prioritizing well-established areas where LLMs are already proficient, such as basic Jetpack Compose best practices.

To learn more, read the official documentation:

  • Android skills
  • Android CLI
  • Android Studio

Install Android skills

Use Android CLI to install a specific skill into the current directory:

android skills add r8-analyzer --project=.

Use Android CLI to install all Android skills to directories for all detected agents:

android skills add --all

If you don't have any existing agent directories and don't specify particular agents, the skills will be installed for Gemini and Antigravity at ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills.

Options:

  • --all - Add all Android skills. If omitted, only the android-cli skill will be installed.
  • --agent - A comma-separated list of agents to install the skill for. If omitted, the skill will be installed for all detected agents.
  • --project - Path to a project root in which to install the skills.

To update all skills or specific ones, run:

android skills update --all
android skills update wear-compose-m3

Install as an agent plugin

Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add android/skills
/plugin install android-skills@android-skills

Codex:

codex plugin marketplace add android/skills
codex plugin add android-skills@android-skills

Activate skills

Your agent automatically activates skills that are relevant to your task. To use a skill, prompt your agent to complete a task that is related to the skill, for example "Make my app UI edge-to-edge." The agent should automatically find and use the skill if it has been installed.

Disclaimer

AI can make mistakes, so always double-check the results.

Contributing

Submit a GitHub issue to provide feedback, report issues, or make new skill requests and changes.

Public contributions are not accepted at this time.

Review our community guidelines

This project follows Google's Open Source Community Guidelines.

Important

BitChord is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to YouTube or Google in any way. Use it at your own discretion.

Features

Playback

  • Search, browse and play anything available on YouTube Music.
  • Hi-Res lossless audio — FLAC/ALAC from a configured module source, with YouTube Music as fallback.
  • Gapless playback with true crossfade, adjustable 0–12s.
  • Automix [Beta] — DJ-style transitions with beat-matching and tempo-stretching.
  • Offline downloads — save tracks with embedded metadata.
  • Local music library integration.
  • Background playback via a proper foreground media session.
  • Apple-like lyrics animation — credit to binimum.

Connectivity & Accounts

  • Sign in with your Google account for personalized content.

  • Spotify integration — connect your account to play your playlists and Liked Songs.

  • Discord Rich Presence — in-app login, live track/artist/album and progress.

  • Scrobbling to Last.fm and ListenBrainz.

  • Playback speed control (0.5×–2.0×) and skip silence.

  • Sleep timer — fixed presets or "stop after this track".

  • System equalizer integration.

  • Bit-perfect USB exclusive output — sends lossless tracks to a USB DAC unchanged, at each track's own rate and bit depth. Thanks to Mornye for the reference.

item.title: rushiranpise/Shizuku-Next
item.description:
A feature-rich Shizuku fork with improved setup, reliability, UI, and additional start methods.

https://rushiranpise.github.io/shizuku-modules/

Shizuku-Next

An enhanced fork of Shizuku that lets apps use system APIs through ADB or root.

About

Shizuku-Next continues development of thedjchi's Shizuku fork, based on the original RikkaApps/Shizuku.

It keeps Shizuku's package name and API, so compatible apps continue to work.

Important: This fork uses a different signing key. Uninstall the official Shizuku or thedjchi's fork before installing Shizuku-Next. A server started by the previous app may remain active until stopped or the device is rebooted.

If you want the original app, visit RikkaApps/Shizuku.

Download

Get the latest build from Releases.

Features

Starting and reliability

  • Start through wireless debugging, USB debugging, root, or the Samsung FOTA-agent system UID path where supported.
  • Automatically handles wireless-debugging pairing, including reading the pairing code on supported devices.
  • Optional start on boot, watchdog restarts, automatic recovery, and configurable restart timing.
  • TCP mode, USB-port recovery, and experimental startup without Wi-Fi on Android 11 to 16.
  • Optional mode to hide Developer options and ADB settings.
  • Clearer startup status, diagnostics, and failure logs.

Manager tools

  • Material 3 interface with Home, Apps, Modules, Labs, and Settings.
  • Manage Shizuku access, app permissions, app ops, battery settings, and app network access, with a fallback to the platform's own firewall API on ROMs whose connectivity command is missing.
  • Inspect app details and launch activities.
  • Built-in shell, log viewer, file browser, and app installer.
  • Manage saved Wi-Fi networks and export/import their credentials.
  • Force dark mode and hide selected device settings for chosen apps.
  • Batch permission changes, searchable app lists, and device information.
  • Tasker and other automation support through intents and status broadcasts.

Firewall

The firewall uses Android's OEM deny chain 3. It can exist from Android 11, but some Android 11 and 12 ROMs do not expose it. The Firewall row appears only after the device answers that the chain is available. Open Labs > Firewall, turn the switch at the top on, then switch on the apps whose network access should be blocked. Work profile and cloned apps appear as their own rows, keyed by user. On Android 13 and newer, the cellular icon beside a blocked app blocks it only on mobile data instead of on every network.

Modules and compatibility

  • Experimental ADB module support, including module actions, services, and WebUI. Writing a module covers the format: module.prop, the environment a script runs in, the WebUI bridge, trust, and how a module gets found.
  • Stealth mode and in-app updates.
  • Android TV and VR-friendly UI support.
  • MediaTek compatibility fixes and improvements for some devices.

Some features are experimental or device-dependent. Root, Samsung FOTA-agent system-UID, and no-Wi-Fi startup methods are not available on every device. Only install modules and scripts you trust.

Requirements

  • Android 7.0 or newer
  • Wireless debugging: Android 11 or newer; supported Android TVs are also compatible.
  • USB/PC start: A computer with ADB.
  • Root start: A rooted device with working root access.
  • System UID start: Samsung devices that ship the FOTA agent (com.sdet.fotaagent). For SMTShell on older One UI, use the Custom command system start.
  • Start on boot: Supported start methods only.

See the wiki for setup and troubleshooting guidance.

Privacy

  • No tracking or analytics.
  • No telemetry or proprietary libraries.
  • No Google Play Services dependency.
  • Open-source code and reproducible builds.
  • Internet access is used for wireless-debugging connections, for checking and downloading GitHub updates, and for the module lists, which are read from GitHub.

The app requests permissions for features such as notifications, background services, wireless debugging, and boot startup. See the app's permission page and source code for details.

Translations

Help translate Shizuku-Next on Crowdin. See docs/translations.md for translation details.

Support the project

Shizuku-Next is free and contains no ads. If you'd like to support development, you can buy me a coffee.

Please also consider supporting the upstream projects: thedjchi and RikkaApps/Shizuku.

Developer guide

API

The API documentation and demo project are available in the Shizuku-API repository.

Shizuku may run with different privileges depending on the start method. Check the server UID and permissions before assuming root access. Prefer ShizukuBinderWrapper over calling transactRemote directly when possible.

Build

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/rushiranpise/Shizuku-Next.git
cd Shizuku-Next
./gradlew :manager:assembleDebug

For a release build, run:

./gradlew :manager:assembleRelease

The debug task builds a debuggable server. In Android Studio, enable Always install with package manager in the Run/Debug configuration when debugging shizuku_server.

Contributing

  1. Fork the repository.
  2. Create a feature branch.
  3. Make and test your changes.
  4. Commit and push your branch.
  5. Open a pull request.

Credits

  • RikkaW / RikkaApps - original Shizuku, server, and API.
  • thedjchi - upstream fork and many inherited features.
  • kerneldroid - Nightzuku, where the ADB modules feature comes from: the module format itself, actions and services, and the window.Shizuku WebUI bridge.
  • Shevery - the published module API and guide this app's module support is written against, and the module catalogue it searches.
  • ShizuWall (AhmetCanArslan) - the firewall's fallback to the system API where a ROM has no connectivity command for it to use, and the technique behind it: the interface reached as Shizuku with a wrapped binder, by reflection.
  • Xhizuku - the other implementation of that format, whose documentation this one is checked against.
  • KernelSU-Next - the card, chip and tab layout the modules list and the Material 3 interface follow.
  • MMRL - the label component whose default accent colour the module cards' size chip follows.
  • All upstream contributors and Crowdin translators.

KernelSU

A kernel-based root solution for Android devices.

Features

  1. Kernel-based su and root access management.
  2. Module system based on metamodules: Pluggable infrastructure for systemless modifications.
  3. App Profile: Lock up the root power in a cage.

Compatibility state

KernelSU officially supports Android GKI 2.0 devices (kernel 5.10+). Older kernels (4.14+) are also supported, but the kernel will need to be built manually.

With this, WSA, ChromeOS, and container-based Android are all supported.

Currently, the arm64-v8a and x86_64 architectures are supported.

Caution

Recent kernel versions have implemented a breaking change causing KernelSU to fail and potentially trigger a kernel panic on x86_64! Check the website for more info!

Translation

To help translate KernelSU, we no longer accept translation contributions via Weblate. All translations are now handled using LLMs.

item.title: SukiSU-Nova/SukiSU-Nova
item.description:
Kernel-based Android Root Solution & KPM

https://SukiSU.org

SukiSU Nova

English 简体中文 |

A kernel-based root solution for Android, evolved from tiann/KernelSU with some interesting changes added.

Features

  1. Kernel-based su and permission management.
  2. App Profile: keep root access in a cage.
  3. KPM support.
  4. Built-in Zygisk (NyaZygisk) — no separate Zygisk module needed; running status is shown right on the home screen.
  5. Theme Store: browse, install and submit themes, with multi-source mirrors, author authorization and review.
  6. Kernel Extension Center: CPU/vvar spoofing, AVC log spoofing, version spoofing, SUSFS and mount view hiding — all in one place.
  7. Built-in SUSFS management tools with one-tap root hiding configuration.
  8. Dual UI: Miuix / Material 3 Expressive; supports Miuix splash screen, module banners and sorting, temporary root grant, and kernel-free preview.

Compatibility

  • SukiSU Nova supports GKI 2.0 devices (kernel version 5.10 and above).
  • Older kernels are also compatible (minimum 4.14+), but you need to compile the kernel yourself.
  • With additional backports, 3.x kernels (3.4–3.18) can be supported.
  • Currently supported architectures: arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a (bare), X86_64, riscv64.
  • Note: This project has evolved independently since forking from tiann/KernelSU; compatibility is based on testing in this repository and no longer equals the official KernelSU support scope.

Kernel Compatibility Status

Scenario Method Notes
GKI devices (kernel 5.10+) LKM mode recommended
Non-GKI / old kernels (3.0+) Compile the kernel manually Please refer to the integration guide on the website
KPM features required Requires CONFIG_KPM=y See "KPM Support" below

KPM Support

Developed based on KernelPatch, with features duplicating KernelSU removed — only KPM support is kept.

Current status:

  • ✅ Basic KPM loading is available (requires CONFIG_KPM=y)
  • 🚧 The APatch compatibility layer is still being completed (some features are not yet merged)
  • ⚠️ Non-GKI devices additionally require CONFIG_KALLSYMS=y and CONFIG_KALLSYMS_ALL=y
  • ⚠️ Kernels below 4.19 need set_memory.h backported from 4.19

Open-source repository: ShirkNeko/SukiSU_KernelPatch_patch
KPM template: udochina/KPM-Build-Anywhere

Troubleshooting

  1. KPM fails to load?
    Make sure the kernel has CONFIG_KPM=y enabled; Non-GKI devices also need CONFIG_KALLSYMS=y and CONFIG_KALLSYMS_ALL=y.

  2. The manager doesn't recognize root?
    Make sure the flashed kernel matches the manager version, and check whether su is in PATH.

  3. Kernel compilation errors?
    Refer to guide/how-to-integrate.md, and make sure the kernel version meets the minimum requirement (4.14+).

Contributing Translations

To translate SukiSU Nova into your language, or improve existing translations, please use Weblate.

Lyrics are provided by LRCLIB and other sources. Sometimes lyrics may not match perfectly with the YouTube videoId parameter. So I need to use some "String Matcher" and "Duration" to search lyrics. So sometimes, some songs or videos get the wrong lyrics.

Simply, because I love the name. It's a combination of 'Simple' and 'Music'. But SimpMusic is not a simple app, it's all you need for a powerful music streaming app.

item.title: RikkaApps/Shizuku
item.description:
Using system APIs directly with adb/root privileges from normal apps through a Java process started with app_process.

Shizuku

Background

When developing apps that requires root, the most common method is to run some commands in the su shell. For example, there is an app that uses the pm enable/disable command to enable/disable components.

This method has very big disadvantages:

  1. Extremely slow (Multiple process creation)
  2. Needs to process texts (Super unreliable)
  3. The possibility is limited to available commands
  4. Even if ADB has sufficient permissions, the app requires root privileges to run

Shizuku uses a completely different way. See detailed description below.

User guide & Download

https://shizuku.rikka.app/

How does Shizuku work?

First, we need to talk about how app use system APIs. For example, if the app wants to get installed apps, we all know we should use PackageManager#getInstalledPackages(). This is actually an interprocess communication (IPC) process of the app process and system server process, just the Android framework did the inner works for us.

Android uses binder to do this type of IPC. Binder allows the server-side to learn the uid and pid of the client-side, so that the system server can check if the app has the permission to do the operation.

Usually, if there is a "manager" (e.g., PackageManager) for apps to use, there should be a "service" (e.g., PackageManagerService) in the system server process. We can simply think if the app holds the binder of the "service", it can communicate with the "service". The app process will receive binders of system services on start.

Shizuku guides users to run a process, Shizuku server, with root or ADB first. When the app starts, the binder to Shizuku server will also be sent to the app.

The most important feature Shizuku provides is something like be a middle man to receive requests from the app, sent them to the system server, and send back the results. You can see the transactRemote method in rikka.shizuku.server.ShizukuService class, and moe.shizuku.api.ShizukuBinderWrapper class for the detail.

So, we reached our goal, to use system APIs with higher permission. And to the app, it is almost identical to the use of system APIs directly.

Developer guide

API & sample

https://github.com/RikkaApps/Shizuku-API

Migrating from pre-v11

Existing applications still works, of course.

https://github.com/RikkaApps/Shizuku-API#migration-guide-for-existing-applications-use-shizuku-pre-v11

Attention

  1. ADB permissions are limited

    ADB has limited permissions and different on various system versions. You can see permissions granted to ADB here.

    Before calling the API, you can use ShizukuService#getUid to check if Shizuku is running user ADB, or use ShizukuService#checkPermission to check if the server has sufficient permissions.

  2. Hidden API limitation from Android 9

    As of Android 9, the usage of the hidden APIs is limited for normal apps. Please use other methods (such as https://github.com/LSPosed/AndroidHiddenApiBypass).

  3. Android 8.0 & ADB

    At present, the way Shizuku service gets the app process is to combine IActivityManager#registerProcessObserver and IActivityManager#registerUidObserver (26+) to ensure that the app process will be sent when the app starts. However, on API 26, ADB lacks permissions to use registerUidObserver, so if you need to use Shizuku in a process that might not be started by an Activity, it is recommended to trigger the send binder by starting a transparent activity.

  4. Direct use of transactRemote requires attention

    • The API may be different under different Android versions, please be sure to check it carefully. Also, the android.app.IActivityManager has the aidl form in API 26 and later, and android.app.IActivityManager$Stub exists only on API 26.

    • SystemServiceHelper.getTransactionCode may not get the correct transaction code, such as android.content.pm.IPackageManager$Stub.TRANSACTION_getInstalledPackages does not exist on API 25 and there is android.content.pm.IPackageManager$Stub.TRANSACTION_getInstalledPackages_47 (this situation has been dealt with, but it is not excluded that there may be other circumstances). This problem is not encountered with the ShizukuBinderWrapper method.

Developing Shizuku itself

Build

  • Clone with git clone --recurse-submodules
  • Run gradle task :manager:assembleDebug or :manager:assembleRelease

The :manager:assembleDebug task generates a debuggable server. You can attach a debugger to shizuku_server to debug the server. Be aware that, in Android Studio, "Run/Debug configurations" - "Always install with package manager" should be checked, so that the server will use the latest code.

License

All code files in this project are licensed under Apache 2.0

Under Apache 2.0 section 6, specifically:

  • You are FORBIDDEN to use manager/src/main/res/mipmap*/ic_launcher*.png image files, unless for displaying Shizuku itself.

  • You are FORBIDDEN to use Shizuku as app name or use moe.shizuku.privileged.api as application id or declare moe.shizuku.manager.permission.* permission.

item.description:
An OSS Android TV client for Jellyfin

Wholphin - an OSS Android TV client for Jellyfin

"Never half-phin two jellies. Always wholphin one jelly."

Wholphin is an open-source Android TV client for Jellyfin. It aims to provide a different app UI that's inspired by Plex for users interested in migrating to Jellyfin.

This is not a fork of the official client. Wholphin's user interface and controls have been written completely from scratch. Wholphin supports playing media using either ExoPlayer or MPV.


Features

User interface

  • Customize the home page to see the content you are interested in
    • Use poster or thumb images, show/hide titles, add/remove/re-order different types of rows!
    • Option to combine the Continue Watching & Next Up into a single row
    • Pin collections, playlists, favorites, genres, and studios
    • Remove series from next up
  • A navigation drawer for quick access to libraries, favorites, search, and settings from almost anywhere in the app
  • Integration with Seerr to discover new movies and TV shows
    • Note: only available when installed from GitHub or the Play store
  • Customize library display
    • Option to show Movie/TV Show titles
    • Choose image types & size
    • Choose from grid or list layouts
  • Play theme music, if available
  • Customize subtitle style for plain text subtitles with separate HDR settings
  • Search & download subtitles (requires compatible server plugin such as OpenSubtitles)
  • Multiple app color themes
  • Protect user profile switches with PIN code or require server login
  • Change the user interface language per user
  • In-app & Android OS screensaver support

Playback

  • Different media playback engines:
    • ExoPlayer w/ optional extra audio, SSA/ASS, & AV1 software decoding
    • MPV for direct playing anything with great SSA/ASS subtitle support
  • Plex inspired playback controls:
    • Using D-Pad left/right for seeking during playback
    • Quickly access video chapters & queue during playback
    • Optionally skip back a few seconds when resuming playback
  • Live TV & DVR support
  • Music & music video support
  • Cinema mode/pre-roll intro support (requires compatible server plugin such as Intros)
  • Auto play next episodes with pass out protection
  • Option for automatic refresh rate & resolution switching on supported displays
  • Trickplay (video preview) support
  • Subtly show playback position along the bottom of the screen while seeking w/ D-Pad

Roadmap

See here for the roadmap

Installation

Using Google Play or Amazon appstore are the fastest way to install. But you can follow these instructions to install without needing an app store

Downloader Code: 8668671

  1. Enable side-loading "unknown" apps

    • https://developer.android.com/distribute/marketing-tools/alternative-distribution#unknown-sources

item.description:
Block ads system-wide on Android using local VPN-based DNS filtering. No root needed. No data collection.

https://blockads.pwhs.app

BlockAds

BlockAds is a free, open-source ad blocker for Android.

It blocks ads, trackers, and malware system-wide using local VPN-based DNS filtering — no root required, no data collection.

Built with Jetpack Compose and Material 3 for a modern, premium experience.





Download



Screenshots

Features

  • Dual Routing Modes: System-wide ad blocking via VPN (no root needed) OR Root Proxy Mode (via iptables)
  • Privacy-first Optional Crash Reporting & Manual Local Logs Export
  • Comprehensive Onboarding Flow (Permissions, Battery Optimization, Opt-in telemetry)
  • WireGuard Profile Import
  • HTTPS Filtering with userspace TCP/IP stack — per-app MITM, cosmetic CSS, JS scriptlets
  • CA cert install verification (auto-refresh after returning from Settings)
  • 284-domain curated passthrough list keeps banking, payments and gov apps working
  • Multiple built-in filter lists (StevenBlack, AdGuard DNS, EasyList, and more)
  • Region-aware defaults — auto-enables filters for your language
  • Real-time DNS query logs with search & filtering
  • Security protection — blocks phishing, malware, and malvertising domains
  • Dark / Light / System theme with Material 3 dynamic colors
  • 7 accent color options + Material You dynamic theming
  • Quick Settings tile & home screen widget
  • Custom block/allow rules and whitelisting
  • Per-app filtering (bypass VPN for selected apps)
  • DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) support with multiple providers
  • Auto-update filter lists on schedule (6h / 12h / 24h / 48h)
  • Export / Import settings backup
  • Auto-reconnect on boot
  • Multi-language support (English, Vietnamese, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Thai, Spanish)
  • 100% local — all data stays on your device

Community

Join our community:

Sponsor

If you enjoy BlockAds, consider supporting the project! Your sponsorship helps us maintain and improve the app.

Build Instructions

Requirements

  • Android Studio Ladybug or newer
  • JDK 17 or higher
  • Android SDK 36 (min SDK 24)
  • (Optional - only needed if modifying Go tunnel) Go 1.23+ and gomobile

Steps

Tip

Historical versions of the Go binary (tunnel.aar) were committed in the past before being moved to GitHub Releases. To avoid downloading ~1.2GB of old binaries, use blobless clone (--filter=blob:limit=1m) to download only ~20MB.

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone --filter=blob:limit=1m https://github.com/pass-with-high-score/blockads-android.git
cd blockads-android

    (Or for a shallow clone: git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/pass-with-high-score/blockads-android.git)

  2. (Optional) Build the Go tunnel AAR/JAR from source (with Android 15 16KB page size support):

    ./scripts/build_tunnel.sh
# Or
./gradlew -Ptunnel.source=local buildGoTunnel

    Note: This is completely optional. Gradle automatically resolves a prebuilt, checksum-pinned tunnel.aar from GitHub Releases by default. You do not need Go or NDK unless you are modifying Go code in tunnel/. See docs/TUNNEL.md.

  3. Open the project in Android Studio

  4. Sync Gradle and run the app on a device or emulator

  5. Build from command line:

    ./gradlew assembleDebug
./gradlew bundleRelease   # requires signing key

How It Works

BlockAds routes DNS queries locally either through a VpnService (Vpn Mode) or via iptables redirection (Root Proxy Mode). These queries are matched against loaded filter lists using a memory-efficient Trie data structure. Matching queries are blocked locally, while all other traffic passes through normally — no data leaves your device.

When HTTPS Filtering is enabled, a userspace TCP/IP stack (gVisor netstack via tun2socks) terminates each TCP/UDP flow in Go, looks up the owning app UID via Android's ConnectivityManager.getConnectionOwnerUid(), and only MITMs flows from selected browsers. Cert-pinned apps and the 284-domain curated passthrough list bypass MITM cleanly. Cosmetic CSS rules and EasyList ##+js(…) / AdGuard #%#//scriptlet(…) scriptlets are injected into HTML responses via a tiny in-memory local asset host.

item.title: Davidona/StreamVault-IPTV
item.description:
StreamVault is a TV-first free IPTV player for Android TV built with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Room, Hilt, and Media3.

StreamVault

StreamVault is a TV-first media player for Android TV built with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Room, Hilt, and Media3.

It is designed for large playlists, remote-friendly browsing, fast provider switching, and a polished living-room playback experience. StreamVault supports M3U playlists, Xtream Codes, Stalker Portal, and Jellyfin providers, plus Stremio-compatible add-ons, with dedicated flows for Live TV, Movies, and Series.

Built for Android TV first, StreamVault focuses on the things generic IPTV apps usually get wrong: D-pad navigation, quick channel movement, large-library organization, and a player that still feels good to use from the couch. Phone and tablet installs are also supported, but the primary UX target is TV.

Preview

Highlights

  • Android TV-first interface with D-pad-friendly focus, navigation, and playback flows
  • Provider support for Xtream Codes, Stalker Portal, Jellyfin, and M3U sources, including local playlist files
  • Combined M3U live-source support with optional in-browser source switching for merged Live TV setups
  • Jellyfin onboarding with password sign-in or Quick Connect QR/code flow for TV-friendly setup
  • Fast live-TV browsing with preview mode, favorites, recent channels, custom groups, and pinned categories
  • Transparent full-guide overlay that can open over live playback without leaving the player
  • Movie and series libraries with detailed info pages, resume support, episode switching, and auto-play for next episodes
  • Offline VOD downloads with grouped episode queues, pause or resume controls, and local playback for completed files
  • Full EPG support with guide search, XMLTV support, and provider archive or catch-up when available
  • Built-in DVR with scheduled recording, background capture, recording playback, and app-managed default storage
  • Multi-view split-screen playback for watching multiple channels at once
  • Plugin API for creating companion Android APKs that extend providers, playback, Cast URL handling, or configuration flows
  • Native Stremio add-on catalogs, metadata, direct/debrid playback, subtitles, resume history, and offline downloads
  • Trakt scrobbling, watched-history sync, watchlists, ratings, custom lists, and Trending or Popular discovery
  • Local and Google Drive backups for provider setup, favorites, groups, and playback history
  • Selectable app themes, subtitle search and customization, and quality controls for VOD playback
  • Strong parental controls with PIN-protected categories and automatic adult-category detection
  • TV integrations including Watch Next, launcher recommendations, TV input sync, Cast support, external-player handoff, and in-app update delivery

Features

Provider Support

  • Xtream Codes
  • Stalker Portal
  • Jellyfin media servers with direct library sync and TV-friendly Quick Connect support
  • M3U playlists from URLs plus local files
  • Play supported adaptive and DRM-protected streams from M3U playlists
  • Expanded Stalker and Ministra compatibility for Live TV, Movies, and Series
  • Quick Stalker setup from supported playback or export links
  • Separate onboarding and sync flows for live channels, movies, series, and guide data
  • Fast switching between providers with provider-scoped settings
  • Combined M3U profiles for merging multiple M3U providers into a single Live TV source
  • Scheduled background refreshes keep saved provider catalogs and guide data up to date
  • QR-based provider pairing from a phone on the same LAN for faster TV setup

Navigation And TV UX

  • Designed for Android TV and D-pad navigation first
  • Fast channel browsing with large-playlist friendly layouts
  • Numeric remote input for direct channel entry
  • Configurable startup landing screen so the app can open Home, Live TV, Movies, Series, Guide, Downloads, Plugins, Stremio-compatible Add-ons, or Settings first
  • Colored remote button remapping with global defaults plus playback and live-browse overrides
  • Customizable Home shelves and primary navigation tabs
  • Preview mode while browsing channels
  • TV-friendly search and text-entry flows

Live TV And Channel Management

  • Favorites and recently watched channels
  • Custom groups for personal channel collections
  • Pinned categories surfaced near the top of the live guide rail
  • Hide or restore individual channels and categories
  • Optional Live TV provider or source browser for M3U-based setups
  • Optional category-sidebar auto-hide and a configurable Live TV clock
  • Long-press live categories for actions like pin, hide, lock or unlock, and custom-group management
  • Channel reordering for favorites and custom groups
  • Channel numbering modes by group or across the full provider lineup
  • Predefined filter words to make category search cleaner on noisy provider data

Guide, Search, And Playback

  • Full EPG grid view
  • Transparent full-guide overlay over live playback
  • Program search inside the guide
  • XMLTV guide support with built-in EPG source management
  • Manual EPG match overrides and source-priority controls from inside Settings and Guide flows
  • Provider archive or catch-up support when the source exposes replay streams
  • Live rewind or timeshift playback with up to 30 minutes of buffer, even when provider catch-up is unavailable
  • Optional real-time translation subtitles while watching supported live streams
  • Global search across live TV, movies, and series
  • Multi-view for watching multiple live streams at once
  • Player controls for subtitles, audio tracks, aspect ratio, playback speed, quality profiles, Cast, and external-player handoff
  • Quality limits by connection or title, with automatic adjustment for supported adaptive streams

Recording And Playback

  • Scheduled and background DVR recording for live channels
  • Record a live stream while watching and save DVR recordings to shared network folders
  • Offline VOD downloads with grouped episode handling and completed-file local playback
  • Program reminders from guide entries when you want a notification without scheduling a recording
  • Recording schedules account for conflicts and recover from interrupted jobs
  • App-managed default recording folder with optional custom storage selection
  • In-app playback for completed recordings with a visible on-player recording indicator during active capture
  • Fine-tune decoder and timeout settings for device compatibility
  • Extra audio-codec support for streams some devices cannot play, with playback diagnostics
  • When a stream fails, automatically try a compatible version and resume with track choices intact

Movies And Series

  • Two VOD layouts:
    • Modern shelf-based browsing
    • Classic left-sidebar category browsing
  • Detailed info pages for movies and series
  • Continue watching, playback history, and detail-screen resume actions with saved position context
  • Search OpenSubtitles, load local SRT files, and customize subtitle timing and appearance
  • Navigate chapters, skip intros and recaps, and start the next episode at the credits
  • Group alternate versions and choose which movie or series version to play
  • Organize M3U entries into Movies or Series, with editable episode groups
  • Pin favorite VOD categories and search Stalker Movies and Series catalogs
  • Long-press VOD categories and custom groups for actions like hide, rename, delete, or reorder when applicable
  • In-player episode switching for series
  • Previous and Next episode controls in the playback overlay
  • Automatic next-episode playback when another episode is available

Parental Controls

  • Hide categories completely
  • Lock categories behind a PIN
  • Option to hide locked content from browsing views
  • Adult-category detection using provider flags and category naming heuristics

Languages And Device Support

  • English plus 37 translated locale packs currently ship with the app
  • Locale coverage is broader and rendering is more reliable across supported languages
  • Built for TV first; phones and tablets are supported, but not the primary design target

Appearance

  • Choose from Classic blue, M3 purple, Light, Forest, Sunset, Ocean, Rose, AMOLED Black, and Vintage themes
  • Modern, theme-aware screens across Live TV, VOD details, search, split screen, and Settings

Platform Integrations

  • Android TV Watch Next integration
  • External launcher item links and TV row integration
  • Launcher recommendations and TV entry points
  • Android TV Input Framework channel sync
  • Google Cast sender support
  • Cast a movie, the resume episode, or a selected episode from its detail page

Plugins

  • StreamVault can be extended with companion Android APK plugins.
  • Plugin developers can expose provider, playback, Cast URL rewrite, and host-rendered or native configuration capabilities.
  • See the StreamVault Plugin API docs to create compatible plugins.

Stremio-compatible Add-ons

  • Install Stremio-compatible add-ons from a manifest URL and browse their catalogs from the Extensions area.
  • Browse catalogs and find metadata, streams, and subtitles across enabled add-ons.
  • Play direct or debrid streams.
  • Save progress, continue watching, and download supported streams for offline playback from Downloads.
  • Plugins and Stremio-compatible Add-ons are grouped under one Extensions navigation item with separate, focusable tabs.
  • Stremio-compatible Add-ons are open by default. Use Settings → Privacy → Hide Stremio-compatible add-ons to hide them independently of IPTV parental controls.

Trakt

  • Sign in to sync watched history and scrobble playback; manage watchlists, ratings, and custom lists, and browse Trending or Popular titles.

Backup And Restore

  • Create and manage local Android TV backups or Google Drive snapshots, then restore providers, favorites, groups, and playback history.
  • New backup exports can include provider credentials so restored providers can sync without entering passwords again.
  • Exported backup files contain provider passwords in readable form; keep them private.

Quick TV Tips

  • Long-press a channel, movie, or series to add it to Favorites or a custom group.
  • Long-press a live category to open category actions such as pin, hide, lock or unlock, and custom-group actions like reorder.
  • In Movies and Series, long-press categories or custom groups for hide or group-management actions where available.
  • Long-press a live channel to queue it for Split Screen.
  • Use the number keys on a remote while in the player to jump directly to a channel.
  • While watching a series, open Episodes in the player to switch episodes without backing out to the details page.

Download

  • Download latest StreamVault.apk
  • On Android TV, use Downloader code 6443624 to get StreamVault.
  • The app can also detect and download newer releases in-app through GitHub Releases.
  • GitHub Actions still runs build and test validation on pushes and pull requests.
  • GitHub Releases are now published only when the workflow is started manually with workflow_dispatch, so versioned releases do not get created by mistake on every push.

Support

If StreamVault is useful to you, you can support development here:

  • Support on Ko-fi

Project Structure

  • app/ Android app UI, navigation, dependency injection, and Android TV integrations
  • data/ Room database, sync, parsing, provider implementations, and repositories
  • domain/ models, repository contracts, managers, and use cases
  • player/ playback abstraction and Media3 player implementation
  • docs/ architecture notes, plugin API docs, and image assets

Build

Requirements:

  • Android Studio
  • Android SDK
  • JDK 17 or another Gradle-supported JDK 17 runtime
  • Android NDK only if you want to rebuild the bundled Media3 FFmpeg extension locally

Useful commands:

./gradlew assembleDebug
./gradlew assembleRelease
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest

Notes

  • StreamVault is an IPTV client, not a content provider.
  • Use only playlists, streams, and guide sources you are authorized to access.
  • Local configuration and signing files are intentionally excluded from git.

License

As of April 2026, all usage, modification, and distribution are governed by the StreamVault Source-Available License (Non-Commercial).

Any use of this project must comply with the terms defined in the LICENSE file.

内嵌浏览器 JCEF 132（Chromium）
视频预览 ffplay（FFmpeg 套件，边下边播）+ JavaFX Media（兜底）

构建分发 Gradle + jlink + jpackage + Inno Setup
Markdown 渲染 multiplatform-markdown-renderer（GFM：README / 更新说明）

使用

  1. 在「网盘」页登录需要使用的网盘账号（推荐内嵌浏览器登录）；视频解析平台的登录在「解析」页对应平台卡片或结果页里完成
  2. 在「解析」页粘贴分享链接或视频链接（可带提取码，支持从剪贴板一键粘贴）
  3. 网盘分享会进入文件浏览页，视频链接会进入结果页（可选清晰度 / 图集 / 预览）
  4. 在「下载」页查看进度，支持暂停 / 继续 / 删除 / 打开；进度同步显示在 Windows 通知中心

设置项、数据目录、托盘操作见 使用说明。

构建

要求：Windows 10/11 x64，另需一个 C++ 编译器（托盘菜单配色桥接层用；缺它时 run / package / installer 会在这一步失败）。JDK、Gradle、Inno Setup 均无需手动安装。

git clone https://github.com/tidain/YunX-Desktop.git
cd YunX-Desktop

.\run.ps1 run        # 编译并启动（开发，含 darkmode.dll）
.\run.ps1 build      # 仅编译 Kotlin（不需要 C++ 编译器）
.\run.ps1 package    # 免安装便携版 → release\YunX-Desktop\
.\run.ps1 installer  # 单文件安装程序 → release\YunX-Desktop-setup-*.exe

环境要求、版本号管理与打包产物见 构建与打包。

常见问题

为什么从「第三方移植」变成了「官方桌面版」？

项目早期确实是社区移植（安卓版 CYQawa/YunX 的 Windows 移植）。 2026 年 10 月 2 日上午 8:40，桌面版作者（tidain）加入安卓版仓库成为协作者， 桌面版自此与安卓版同属一个项目，作为云析的官方 Windows 桌面端维护； 两端的代码、发布节奏与分发方式仍各自独立。

百度网盘下载 / 转存不了？

账号被风控了，详见安卓版 issue #9。

便携版和安装版有什么区别？

便携版是免安装的文件夹，拷到任意位置双击 YunX-Desktop.exe 即可运行； 安装版走安装向导，安装到 %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\YunX-Desktop，并创建开始菜单 / 桌面快捷方式，可在设置中卸载。 两者功能完全一致。

下载时看不到 Windows 通知中心的通知？

先确认「设置 → 系统 → 通知」已开启（专注助手 / 免打扰也会拦通知）。应用在检测到通知未送达时， 会尝试自动创建所需的开始菜单快捷方式兜底，但最终能否弹出仍取决于系统通知设置。

Andee

Anything you can do, it can — and it becomes the soul of the device.

Not the assistant that helps you operate your phone — not a tool, not a companion.

What moves in is not an app on the phone.

A phone, a Mac, a tablet — each is a body it lives in. And the Andees on different devices can be friends.

No root. No custom ROM. One APK on Android, one app on the Mac.

Andee is a personal agent

Tell it what you want. It does it on your phone and on your Mac, the way you would: it opens the app, taps, types, reads the screen. When a job is long, it hands it to a helper and keeps talking to you. It remembers you, and it keeps working when you are not asking.

This is the shape DeepSeek calls a Super Agent: one agent that talks to you and keeps track of everything, and helpers that go off and do the long work. DeepSeek built theirs for a team's GitHub repository and says it is a research prototype. Andee is the same idea for one person, on the devices they already use.

Andee OpenClaw ChatGPT dots Gemini on the phone
Runs on your own phone and Mac your own Mac, Windows or Linux OpenAI's cloud, each with its own cloud computer Google's cloud
Works in any phone app, without the app doing anything Yes not stated not stated only supported apps, a few phones, US and Korea, beta
Works your computer Yes files, shell, browser can link one computer no
Remembers you between chats Yes, in a notebook that stays on your device yes yes not stated
Acts when you have not asked Yes, with an off switch not stated not stated recurring tasks
Hands long jobs to a helper while you keep talking Yes (works from the Mac; phone to Mac not yet tested on a device) not stated not stated not stated
Open source Yes Yes No No

"Not stated" means their own pages do not say. It does not mean they cannot. The other columns come from OpenClaw's page, a comparison of nine assistants and a report on Gemini and Siri, read in November 2026. Products change; check theirs.

What it does

  • Any app, nothing to set up in the app. It looks at the screen and taps like you do. On the Mac it also uses windows and a terminal, and asks you first before anything risky. If you can do it with your thumb, it can.
  • Long jobs go to a helper. Research, a code repository, a pile of files, a command that runs for an hour. Andee gives it to an agent on your Mac (DeepSeek Harness) and keeps talking to you. When it is done, the files show up in the app and you open them there. Your phone can use the Mac's agent too.
  • It keeps track of what it took on. Who it is waiting for, whether they answered, what it delivered. A job stays on the list until you say it is done, not when Andee says so.
  • It reads your notifications first. It handles the ones you asked it to, tells you about the ones that matter in one sentence, and drops the rest.
  • It logs in for you without knowing your password. The vault types it into the box. No tool can read it back.

Why it is not a phone assistant

A phone assistant waits for you to ask. Andee does not wait.

  • It has its own notebook. Who it is, what it cares about, the people it knows, a diary. It stays on your device. You can read every entry and delete any of them.
  • It works when you are not asking. When a conversation goes quiet it looks back over it and finishes what it promised. It checks for things that have waited too long and works on them, with the same tools it has when you ask, but quietly: it does not speak, and what it did shows up in your timeline. You can turn this off in Settings, and one tap on the ball stops everything it is doing. What it may send to people, spend or delete is limited by rules, not by a lock. SECURITY.md says where those rules stop being enough.
  • It stays quiet by default. A notification is either handled, mentioned in one line, or dropped with a note saying why. A message from a stranger cannot open your vault, no matter what it says. That check is in the code, not in the prompt.
  • It has its own face and voice. Six looks and nineteen moods, and the model chooses the face as it speaks.
  • It has friends. The Andees on your own devices can ask each other for help. So can someone else's, if its owner agrees, and then the job runs where it cannot see your memory.

It lives in two places today, an Android phone or tablet and a Mac, and it can drive a small robot dog. It is the same Andee on both.

Install

Easiest: build it on CodeFlying. Open the page, tap build, scan the code to download. The package already has the model and voice keys in it, so it can talk as soon as it is installed. New accounts get a free allowance, then you pay for tokens. (中文：codeflying.net/andee.) CodeFlying is a separate service with its own terms, prices and data handling.

Or download a release from GitHub:

Device File After installing
Android phone or tablet (Android 8.1+) andee-<version>-en-android-arm64-v8a.apk (nearly every device) turn on Overlay, then Accessibility
Mac, Apple silicon (macOS 14+) andee-<version>-en-mac-arm64.dmg drag Andee to Applications; allow Accessibility and Screen Recording when asked
Mac, Intel andee-<version>-en-mac-x64.dmg same

Release files have no keys in them. Put your CodeFlying key in ⚙ → Backend, or switch to On-device and enter your own model and voice keys. Then tap the ball and talk. Permissions explains why each one is needed and what happens if you say no. Getting started is the short first-run guide.

You can check all of this

There is no analytics SDK and no tracking of what you say. The only thing that reaches the maintainers is the update check: the version number, phone model and brand, system version, interface language and a random install ID. The whole agent loop is in this repository, including the parts that stop it from doing harm: the vault, the turns that cannot touch it, the commands that need your yes. Where it falls short is written down in SECURITY.md and the disclaimer.

Build it yourself · Everything it can do, how it is built, the wake word, the robot dog · Changelog · Contributing · Report a vulnerability, privately

Showcase

Built something with it? Show us. The ones worth collecting are usually the ones nobody planned — the odd workaround, the thing it turned out to be able to do, the one that made you laugh. It does not have to be useful.

Post it in Show and tell, one case per post, so each one can be discussed on its own. Three things make a post useful to the next person:

  • What it ran on — device, Android version, ROM. This app talks to Android at a level where ROMs disagree, so "worked on my phone" tells a reader almost nothing.
  • What you asked for, and what it actually did — the sentence you really said is more interesting than a summary of it.
  • A link, if you have one — YouTube, Bilibili, X, your own blog, anything public. GitHub cannot play a video inside a README, so it will be a clickable link rather than a player. On YouTube you can make it a thumbnail that looks like one:

(substitute the id from the video's URL — youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID)

One thing here is not a formality: this app reads the screen. A screenshot or a recording is a picture of your messages, your notifications, and whatever else happened to be open at the time. Blur or avoid anything private — yours or anyone else's — before it goes up.

Contributing

  • Code — read CONTRIBUTING.md (Chinese) first. It covers the code style, and the rules for the three different kinds of Chinese in this codebase (only one of them is translated). Changing a persona or a mood has its own section there; that is not ordinary copy.
  • Bugs — the issue tracker wants your device, Android version, ROM and logcat. This app talks to Android at a level where ROMs disagree: a call that works on AOSP can fail silently on MagicOS. Without that, most reports cannot be reproduced.
  • Personas and looks — a new look writes tone and nothing else; capabilities belong to the rulebook, not to a character.
  • Docs and translations — welcome. Both READMEs are now self-contained, so either one can be corrected on its own; the Chinese one is the one that has to stay accurate for provisioning, since it is the one most installers will read.

Contributors

Community & contact

Channel Use it for
Issue tracker Reproducible bugs, engineering work
Show and tell What you built with it, fun or not — see Showcase
Security Vulnerabilities — privately, never in a public issue. See SECURITY.md
Product / online Trying Andee without building it yourself — codeflying.app · codeflying.net
WeChat Add Andee as a friend — scan the code below, or tap the WeChat icon at the foot of the chat

Security disclosure

Please do not open a public issue for a security problem. The private reporting channel and the process are in SECURITY.md.

That document also lists the known limitations you should read before deploying this, including one that matters on any network you do not control: the debug WebSocket server binds 0.0.0.0:9008 and does not authenticate its clients. docs/permissions.md (Chinese) explains each permission against a concrete tool, and SECURITY.md is honest about what is not fixed yet.

Disclaimer and acceptable use

Two documents, and both are conditions of use rather than formalities. Each has a Chinese counterpart (*.zh-CN.md), linked from the top of the file:

  • DISCLAIMER.md (Chinese) — what this software is (experimental, no SLA, no warranty), exactly where your data goes, what it is actually capable of, and who bears the consequences.
  • docs/acceptable-use.md (Chinese) — the prohibited uses. Violating them exceeds the licence and terminates it automatically.

The four points worth reading even if you read nothing else:

  • It can spend money. There is no payment tool, and there does not need to be — it taps. The only thing blocking a completed transfer is Android's own FLAG_SECURE; this project has no guardrail on that path. Keep a human present for anything financial, and treat "the AI did it" as no defence, because it is not one.
  • What it sends is yours. Messages, posts, calls and orders go out under your name.
  • Your data leaves the device. There is no analytics SDK in this repo — but speech goes to whichever speech provider you select (Volcengine by default, Google if you pick it), the conversation plus every tool result goes to whichever brain endpoint you configure, and the version check goes to a server the maintainers run. Local mode changes the destination, not the fact.
  • It can be steered by what is on screen. Anyone who can get you to open a page can influence it.

License

Apache-2.0 with additional conditions — no multi-tenant SaaS, no white-labelling that removes the branding, and no embedding it in another product without written authorisation. GitHub reports this as NOASSERTION; that is expected, not a misconfiguration.

Bundled third-party components are inventoried in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Read it before redistributing: the ML Kit barcode SDK and the play-services-* stubs are not open-source, and the barcode model is fetched from Google at runtime.

See CHANGELOG.md for what changed and for the versioning policy. The latest release is v0.17.0 — pre-1.0 on purpose, because the wire contract and the build flags are still moving.

Andee

任何你能做的事情它都能，它会成为这台设备的主人。

他不是那种帮你操作手机的助手，也不是工具或伙伴 ——
住进来的不是一个 App，是一个灵魂。
手机、Mac、平板，都是他住进去的身体；不同设备上的 Andee，还能成为朋友。
不用 root，不用刷机，不用插着电脑。Android 上一个 APK，Mac 上一个 App。

Andee 是你的 Personal Agent

你跟它说想要什么，它就在你的手机和 Mac 上去做，跟你自己做一样：打开 App、点、打字、看屏幕。活儿太长，它就交给 帮手去干，自己继续跟你说话。它记得你，你没叫它的时候，它也在干活。

这就是 DeepSeek 说的 Super Agent：一个对着你、替你记账的 agent，加一群去干长活的帮手。DeepSeek 做的那个是给团队的 GitHub 仓库用的，他们自己说只是研究原型。Andee 是同一个 思路，给一个人用，装在他每天用的设备上。

Andee OpenClaw（小龙虾） WorkBuddy 豆包手机
跑在哪 你自己的手机和 Mac 你自己的 Mac、Windows、Linux 腾讯说操作在本地电脑完成 字节和中兴做的手机，助手在系统里
能在手机任何 App 里操作，App 不用做任何适配 能 没说 没说；手机端用来远程指挥电脑 第一代能；据晚点报道，新一代对头部 App 改成谈合作
能操作你的电脑 能 文件、命令行、浏览器 文件、PPT、浏览器 不适用
跨对话记得你 能，记在你设备上的小本本里 能 没说 没说
你没开口它也行动 能，可以关 没说 能，可设定时任务 没说
长活交给帮手，自己继续陪你 能（Mac 上能用；手机连 Mac 还没在真机上测过） 没说 没说 没说
开源 是 是 否 否

「没说」是指它们自己的页面没讲，不等于做不到。其余几列来自 OpenClaw 的页面、 WorkBuddy 的腾讯云介绍和 媒体对豆包手机的报道（转述晚点 LatePost 7 月 17 日的消息）， 2026 年 11 月读的。产品每个月都在变，请以它们自己为准。

它能替你做什么

  • 任何 App，App 那边什么都不用做。 它看着屏幕，像你一样点。在 Mac 上它还能用窗口和终端，有风险的先问你。 你用手指能做的，它就能做。
  • 长活交给帮手。 查资料、改一个代码仓库、处理一堆文件、跑一个小时的命令。Andee 把它交给你 Mac 上的 agent （DeepSeek Harness），自己继续跟你说话。做完以后，文件在 App 里列出来， 点开就能看。手机也能用 Mac 上的 agent。
  • 它记着接下的事。 在等谁、对方回了没有、交付了什么。一件事一直留在清单里，直到你说办完了，不是 Andee 自己说了算。
  • 通知先过它这一关。 你交代过要它回的，它去回；要紧的，一句话告诉你；其余的丢掉。
  • 它替你登录，但不知道你的密码。 保险箱把密码填进输入框，没有任何工具能把它读出来。

为什么它不是手机助手

手机助手等你开口。Andee 不等。

  • 它有自己的小本本。 他是谁、在意什么、认识的人、日记。都在你的设备上。每一条你都能看，都能删。
  • 你没叫它，它也在干活。 聊完安静下来，它会回头看一遍，把答应过的事做完。也会去看有什么放太久了，去处理。 用的是你叫它做事时同样的工具，但是安静地做：不出声，做了什么会写在你的动态里。你可以在设置里关掉，点一下球，它手上的 事全都停。至于它能替你发给谁、花多少钱、删什么，靠的是规则，不是一把锁。规则哪里不够，SECURITY.md 里写了。
  • 它默认不吵你。 一条通知，要么处理，要么一句话告诉你，要么丢掉并记下为什么。陌生人发来的消息，不管怎么写， 都打不开你的保险箱。这个检查写在代码里，不是写在提示词里。
  • 它有自己的脸和声音。 六个形象、十九种情绪，说话的时候由模型自己挑表情。
  • 它有朋友。 你不同设备上的 Andee 可以互相求助。别人的 Andee 也可以，只要主人同意；这样活就跑在看不到你记忆的地方。

现在它住在两个地方，一台 Android 手机或平板，和一台 Mac，还能带一只小机器狗。两边是同一个 Andee。

安装

最省事：到 CodeFlying 一键打包。 打开页面点「立即打包」，扫码下载。包里已经配好了 模型和语音密钥，装上就能说话。新用户有免费额度，用完要买。（English：codeflying.app/andee。） CodeFlying 是独立的服务，条款、价格和数据怎么处理，都由它自己定。

也可以直接下载发布包，在 GitHub Releases：

设备 下载哪个 装好之后
Android 手机或平板（Android 8.1+） andee-<版本>-zh-android-arm64-v8a.apk（几乎所有设备） 开悬浮窗，再开无障碍
Mac，Apple 芯片（macOS 14+） andee-<版本>-zh-mac-arm64.dmg 把 Andee 拖进「应用程序」；它要「辅助功能」和「屏幕录制」时允许
Mac，Intel andee-<版本>-zh-mac-x64.dmg 同上

发布包里没有密钥。在 ⚙ → 后端 里填 CodeFlying 的密钥，或者切到「本机」填你自己的模型和语音密钥。然后点那颗球，说话。 每项权限为什么要、拒绝了会怎样，见权限；第一次上手看入门指南。

这些你可以自己查

没有数据分析 SDK，也不追踪你说了什么。会到维护者手上的只有版本自检：版本号、手机型号和品牌、系统版本、界面语言， 加一个随机安装 ID。整个 agent 的循环都在这个仓库里，包括那些防它做坏事的部分：保险箱、碰不到保险箱的那些轮次、要你点头才能跑的命令。 它在哪里做得不够，写在 SECURITY.md 和免责声明里。

自己构建 · 它能做的一切、怎么搭的、唤醒词、机器狗 · 变更记录 · 参与贡献 · 私下报告漏洞

好玩的用法

用它做过什么？说来听听。 值得收的往往不是"正经用途"—— 是你绕的那个弯、是它居然真能做成的 那件事、是把你逗乐的那一下。不实用也可以。

发到 Show and tell， 一个帖子讲一个，这样每个都能单独聊。想让下一个人看得懂，三件事最好带上：

  • 跑在什么机器上 —— 机型、Android 版本、ROM。这个应用和 Android 打交道的层次上，各家 ROM 是 有分歧的，"我手机上能用"对别人几乎等于没说。
  • 你说了什么，它真做了什么 —— 你原话那句，往往比概括出来的有意思。
  • 有链接就贴 —— YouTube、B站、微博、自己的博客，公开的就行。GitHub 的 README 放不了视频 播放器，它只能是个可点的链接。YouTube 的话可以做成缩略图，看起来就像个播放器：

  • 报 bug —— 请务必带上设备型号、Android 版本、ROM 和 logcat。这个应用和 Android 打交道的 层次上各家 ROM 是有分歧的：AOSP 上能用的调用在 MagicOS 上可能静默失败。缺这些，多数报告没法 复现。
  • 形象与人设 —— 新形象只写语气，不写能力。能力属于行为准则，不属于某个角色。
  • 文档与翻译 —— 欢迎。中文 README 是装机那份，必须保持准确。

微信 加 Andee 为好友 —— 扫下面的码，或者点聊天页底部的微信图标

安全披露

安全问题请不要开公开 issue。私密上报渠道和处理流程在 SECURITY.md。

那份文件同时列出了部署前必须知道的已知限制，其中一条在任何你控制不了的网络上都成立：调试 用的 WebSocket 服务绑在 0.0.0.0:9008 且不验证客户端身份。本应用申请的权限组合与安卓银行木马 的检测特征高度重合 —— docs/permissions.zh-CN.md 把每一条对应到一个具体工具， 而 SECURITY.md 对"还没修的"是诚实的。

免责声明与可接受使用

两份文件，都是使用条件，不是客套。中文版在这里，英文版见各自的对照文件：

item.title: LSPosed/LSPrivilege
item.description:
LSPrivilege

中文

LSPrivilege is a modular Android kernel privilege-escalation app for gaining temporary root on supported kernels and loading root managers such as KernelSU or APatch. It is designed to support multiple exploit backends rather than targeting a single vulnerability (currently shipping CVE-2026-43499, with additional backends planned).

Use the app

  1. Install a root manager APK from KernelSU, SukiSU Ultra, BakaSU/ReSukiSU, KowSU, or APatch.
  2. Install the LSPrivilege APK and open it.
  3. Check that your kernel is supported, then tap Run.

Support requires an exact uname -r match. Check the supported devices for your kernel build.

If Shizuku is enabled, start it with ADB before running LSPrivilege. Tap LSPrivilege's status card to grant access.

Any root manager that ships libksud.so or libapd.so provides ksud/apd for module loading. The built-in list (KernelSU, SukiSU Ultra, ReSukiSU, BakaSU, KowSU, APatch) is auto-detected, and other managers can be picked in Settings → Root manager. Without ksud/apd, W1/W2 still grant uid 0 but no module is loaded.

Add a kernel profile

You can import a profile without rebuilding the app:

  • Parse OTA link accepts a full OTA ZIP URL.
  • Parse local image accepts boot.img and an optional xbl_config.img.
  • Import offsets.conf (v2) accepts a HOCON profile. Import offsets.json (v1) converts an older JSON report in the app.

Extractor output is an unverified candidate. The app checks missing or invalid fields before execution. Generating a profile does not prove device support. See the porting guide for validation and built-in registration.

See the MediaTek guide for image-based address recovery and the rooted-device fallback.

Command-line tools

Run the native binary with an exported profile

Requires the Android NDK, make, Gradle, and ADB. An adb shell run skips the app's seccomp bypass stage.

make -C src lsprivilege
./gradlew exportKernelProfiles
adb push build/native/lsprivilege /data/local/tmp/lsprivilege
adb push "build/kernel-profiles/<release>.bin" /data/local/tmp/profile.bin
adb shell chmod 755 /data/local/tmp/lsprivilege
adb shell /data/local/tmp/lsprivilege --load-prebuilt-profile /data/local/tmp/profile.bin
Build and run the offset extractor

Requires Rust. The extractor accepts a boot image, a full OTA ZIP, or an HTTP(S) URL.

(cd tools/extract_rs && cargo build --release)
build/extract/release/lsprivilege-extract boot.img --xbl-config xbl_config.img --format conf --out profile.conf
build/extract/release/lsprivilege-extract OTA.zip --format conf --out profile.conf

Import profile.conf in the app. Omit --xbl-config if you do not have that image. The extractor rejects a patched remove_waiter() with exit code 6.

Reference

  • Native core
  • Add a component, engineering rules, and writing rules

item.title: andreknieriem/open-headunit
item.description:
Headunit App for displaying Android Auto

https://headunit.andrerinas.com/

Open Headunit

Open Headunit is an Android app that allows you to turn your Android tablet or phone into an Android Auto receiver. This project is a revived version of the original headunit project by the great Michael Reid. The original project can be found here: https://github.com/mikereidis/headunit

It runs on Android 4.1 and newer (Android 5.0 and newer for the Play Store build). Besides the stores above, you can download APKs from the Releases page.

Contents: How to use · Known Issues · Planned · Changelog · Contributing

NOTE!

Android Auto 17.4 and newer can prevent legacy wireless triggers from launching projection, including Self-Mode and automated startup via Wireless Helper. Rooted devices have a workaround: re-enable Android Auto's wireless startup receiver. Use a USB wireless dongle, Native Mode or the Headunit Server instead. Wireless Helper works up to Android Auto 17.3, or on 17.4+ with the root workaround. See Wireless Connection Options.

Screenshots

How to use

Check out the Wiki for detailed documentation, setup guides and troubleshooting!

Wired USB Connection

  • Connect your Android device (phone) to the tablet running Open Headunit via USB cable.
  • Make sure that Android Auto is installed on your phone.
  • Set your phone to Host-Mode if necessary and select Android Auto
  • Click the USB Button in Open Headunit, find your phone and click the right button to allow connection
  • Click on your phone in the list and wait for Android Auto to start

Once a phone is set up, plugging it in connects by itself. You can change this in the Auto-start settings with Connect when plugged in.

Wireless Connection Options

Choose from the five options below depending on your Android Auto version and setup:

1. USB Wireless Android Auto Dongle (Most Reliable)

  • A standard hardware USB Wireless Android Auto Dongle (plugged into the headunit) handles the entire wireless negotiation independently.
  • Provides seamless plug-and-play connection regardless of phone Android Auto version.

2. Native Mode (Wi-Fi Direct / Headunit Hotspot)

  • Directly communicates with Android Auto's native wireless protocol without helper apps.
  • Supports Wi-Fi Direct (P2P) or the Headunit Hotspot transport.
  • Configure under Open Headunit Settings -> Wireless Connection -> Wireless Mode -> Native.
  • Native Mode starts over Bluetooth, then moves to WiFi. Detect automatically fits most units. Units that keep Bluetooth on a separate module, or that use a relay, take one of these routes:
    • ZLink module (experimental): units with a ZJ/ZLink Bluetooth service on port 3152.
    • ZJ socket: Unisoc units whose module uses /dev/socket/zj_bt_socket.
    • FYT BLINK module (experimental): FYT units with a separate module, such as DUDUAUTO on DUDUOS.
    • HCT service: units with a verified HCT Bluetooth service, without root. The app detects it by itself.
    • ESP32 relay: an original ESP32 relays the handshake. Firmware: aa-native-bt-broker-for-openheadunit.

3. Headunit Server (No-Root Option for Self-Mode on AA 17.4+)

  • Starts the native Android Auto developer server directly on your phone or on the same device (Self-Mode).
  • Setup:
    1. Open Android Auto settings on your phone (or tablet in Self-Mode).
    2. Scroll down and tap Version 10 times to unlock Developer settings.
    3. Tap the three-dot menu in the top right corner and choose Start headunit server.
    4. In Open Headunit, tap the WiFi button to connect (or use Self-Mode).

4. Wireless Helper

  • Our companion app triggers the wireless connection automatically in the background.
  • Compatibility: Android Auto v17.3 and below, or v17.4+ with the root workaround in option 5.
  • Download: Wireless Helper on Google Play Store
  • Setup: Set Open Headunit Wireless Mode to Wireless Helper, ensure both devices are in the same network or Wi-Fi Direct group, and start the service in the Wireless Helper app.

5. Root Workaround for Android Auto 17.4+

On a rooted device running Android Auto, one shell command restores the previous wireless startup flow, so Wireless Helper keeps working. See the command and its limits.

Optional automatic Wi-Fi scan pause

This is a setting, not a way to connect. On Android 8 and newer, Open Headunit can pause Android's automatic Wi-Fi searches during a Native wireless connection, through Shizuku. It is off by default. See the setup and limits per Android version.

Connect Wirelessly via Intent (Power Users)

You can trigger a wireless connection attempt using an Android Intent. This is useful for automation tools like Tasker, MacroDroid, or via ADB.

URI Scheme: headunit://connect?ip=<PHONE_IP>

Example ADB Command:

adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "headunit://connect?ip=192.168.1.25"

The Automation guide lists every command.

Known Issues

  • Google Maps in Portrait Mode: Touch interactions (searching, scrolling) within Google Maps may not work as expected when using Portrait Mode on some devices. Fix: Try reducing the Pixel density (DPI) setting to below 200 (e.g., 190) in the app settings. This often restores full functionality.
  • Wireless Connection Drops: If the connection drops frequently, disable "WiFi Assistant" or "Switch between networks" in your phone's WiFi settings to prevent it from killing the connection due to "no internet." Check battery saving options.
  • Self-mode on Android 10 (Q) and below: Google has disabled the automatic wireless projection startup for Android 10 and below in Android Auto versions 16.4 and higher. While Self-mode still works on newer Android versions, it is normally impossible to trigger projection on Android 10 and below directly with recent Google app updates. Workaround: You can still use Self-mode on these devices by starting the built-in Android Auto Headunit Server and connecting via Wi-Fi mode (loopback). See the Troubleshooting Guide for step-by-step instructions.
  • Reconnect does nothing until Bluetooth is restarted (Native Mode, Android 12 and older): After a session ends, the hands-free link to the phone can go dead — the phone stops answering wake pokes, and only toggling Bluetooth on the phone or the unit (or restarting the app) recovers it. Open Headunit now notices the repeated failures and cycles this unit's own Bluetooth radio once per attempt, because Android Auto only starts wireless when it sees a Bluetooth connection change. That lever does not exist from Android 13 on, where BluetoothAdapter.disable() is a no-op — there the phone has to raise the connection itself. Fix: make sure the phone's Bluetooth is on, then open Settings → Wireless Connection → Re-measure the Bluetooth wake to clear a stored result that may be holding the cycle back.
  • WiFi Direct takes a long time to connect: One user traced this to Google Assistant in Android Auto. With Gemini on newer Android Auto versions it runs smoothly again. We do not know why.
  • Stuck on "Android Auto is starting": Check your video codec in the settings, and set it to H.264 if your device does not support H.265. Some devices have a broken H.265 decoder, which leaves the app stuck on this message.

  • more customization options for the UI and the app itself
  • Carplay Integration

Then set the passwords as environment variables, for example in ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc:

export HEADUNIT_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD="YOUR_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
export HEADUNIT_KEY_PASSWORD="YOUR_KEY_PASSWORD"

Headunit for Android Auto (tm)

A new car or a $600+ headunit is NOT required to enjoy the integration and distraction reduced environment of Android Auto.

This headunit app can turn a Android 4.1+ tablet supporting USB Host mode into a basic Android Auto compatible headunit.

item.title: aistra0528/Hail
item.description:
Disable / Hide / Suspend / Uninstall Android apps without root.

English | 简体中文 | 日本語

Hail 雹

Hail is a free-as-in-freedom software to freeze Android apps. GitHub Releases

Freeze

Freeze is a word that describes the action of blocking (immediately stopping) apps when they are not needed/in-use ( on-demand request) which in turn helps the device to cut down on the usage of RAM and save power. Users can also unfreeze them to revert to their original state.

In general, "freeze" means disable, but also Hail can "freeze" apps by hiding and suspending them.

Disable

Disabled apps will not be shown in the launcher and will be shown as "Disabled" in the installed apps list. Enable them to revert the action.

Hide

Hidden apps will not be shown in the launcher and in the installed apps list. Unhide them to revert the action.

While in this state, which is almost like an uninstalled state, the package will be unavailable, however, the application data and the actual package file will not be removed from the device.

Suspend (Android 7.0+)

Suspended apps will have their icons shown in grayscale within the device's launcher. Unsuspend them to revert the action.

While in this state, the application's notifications will be hidden, any of its started activities will be stopped and it will not be able to show toasts, dialogs or even play audio. When the user tries to launch a suspended app, the system will, instead, show a dialog to the user informing them that they cannot use this app while it is suspended.

Suspend only prevents the user from interacting with the app, it does NOT prevent the app from running in the background.

Working mode

Any app that has been frozen on Hail will need to be unfrozen by the same working mode.

  1. For devices supporting wireless debugging (Android 11+) or rooted devices, Shizuku is recommended.

  2. For rooted devices, Root is an alternative. It is slower.

Privilege Force Stop Disable Hide Suspend Uninstall/Reinstall (System Apps)
Root ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
Device Owner ✗ ✗ ✓ ✓ ✗
Privileged System App ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗ ✗
Shizuku (root)/Sui ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
Shizuku (adb) ✓ ✓ ✗ ✓ ✓
Dhizuku ✗ ✗ ✓ ✓ ✗
Island/Insular ✗ ✗ ✓ ✓ ✗

Device Owner

You must remove Hail as a device owner before you can uninstall it

Set device owner by adb

Android Debug Bridge (adb) Guide

Download Android SDK Platform-Tools

Issue adb command:

adb shell dpm set-device-owner com.aistra.hail/.receiver.DeviceAdminReceiver

In response, adb prints this message if device owner has been successfully set:

Success: Device owner set to package com.aistra.hail. Active admin set to component {com.aistra.hail/com.aistra.hail.receiver.DeviceAdminReceiver}

Search the message by search engine otherwise.

Remove device owner

Settings > Remove Device Owner

Privileged System App

The following privapp-permissions is required:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<permissions>
    <privapp-permissions package="com.aistra.hail">
        <permission name="android.permission.PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS"/>
        <permission name="android.permission.FORCE_STOP_PACKAGES"/>
        <permission name="android.permission.CHANGE_COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE"/>
        <permission name="android.permission.MANAGE_APP_OPS_MODES"/>
    </privapp-permissions>
</permissions>

To use this mode, you should install Hail as a privileged system app.

The recommended approach is to import Hail when building your ROM, here's an example for Android.bp:

android_app_import {
    name: "Hail",
    apk: "Hail.apk",
    privileged: true,

    dex_preopt: {
        enabled: false,
    },
    presigned: true,
    preprocessed: true,

    required: ["privapp-permissions_com.aistra.hail.xml"]
}

prebuilt_etc {
    name: "privapp-permissions_com.aistra.hail.xml",
    src: "privapp-permissions.xml",
    sub_dir: "permissions",
}

Revert

By adb

Replace com.package.name to the package name of target app.

# Enable app
adb shell pm enable com.package.name
# Unhide app (root required)
adb shell su -c pm unhide com.package.name
# Unsuspend app
adb shell pm unsuspend com.package.name

Modify file

Access /data/system/users/0/package-restrictions.xml, this file stores the restrictions about apps. You can modify, rename or just delete it.

  • Enable app: Modify the value of enabled from 2 (DISABLED) or 3 (DISABLED_USER) to 1 (ENABLED)

  • Unhide app: Modify the value of hidden from true to false

  • Unsuspend app: Modify the value of suspended from true to false

Wipe data by recovery

None of my business 😦

API

adb shell am start -a action -e key value

action can be one of the following constants:

  • com.aistra.hail.action.LAUNCH: Unfreeze and launch target app. If it is unfrozen, it will launch directly. key="package" value="com.package.name"

  • com.aistra.hail.action.FREEZE: Freeze target app. It must be checked at Home. key="package" value="com.package.name"

  • com.aistra.hail.action.UNFREEZE: Unfreeze target app. key="package" value="com.package.name"

  • com.aistra.hail.action.FREEZE_TAG: Freeze all non-whitelisted apps in the target tag. key="tag" value="Tag name"

  • com.aistra.hail.action.UNFREEZE_TAG: Unfreeze all apps in the target tag. key="tag" value="Tag name"

  • com.aistra.hail.action.FREEZE_ALL: Freeze all apps at Home. extra is not necessary.

  • com.aistra.hail.action.UNFREEZE_ALL: Unfreeze all apps at Home. extra is not necessary.

  • com.aistra.hail.action.FREEZE_NON_WHITELISTED: Freeze all non-whitelisted apps at Home. extra is not necessary.

  • com.aistra.hail.action.FREEZE_AUTO: Auto freeze apps at Home. extra is not necessary.

  • com.aistra.hail.action.LOCK: Lock screen. extra is not necessary.

  • com.aistra.hail.action.LOCK_FREEZE: Freeze all apps at Home and lock screen. extra is not necessary.

or use following schema:

  • hail://launch?package=xxx

  • hail://freeze?package=xxx

  • hail://unfreeze?package=xxx

  • hail://freeze_tag?tag=xxx

  • hail://unfreeze_tag?tag=xxx

  • hail://freeze_all

  • hail://unfreeze_all

  • hail://freeze_non_whitelisted

  • hail://freeze_auto
